clue.text: Much appreciated disruption of hunt? Okay

indicators.note: a disruption throws things into disorder, so the letters of the two following words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone thanks a person for breaking up a hunt, which they approve of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disruption of' rearranges the eight letters of HUNT and OKAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A grateful phrase said when something is much appreciated; the two are equivalent expressions of gratitude.

clue.text: Veronese in pretty Baltimore collection

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the run of letters of the following words, a collection of letters

explanation.surface: A painting by the artist Veronese is held in a pleasant Baltimore gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Veronese' suggests the painter, but means a man of Verona: Juliet's hot-headed cousin in Romeo and Juliet.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet is set in Verona, and Juliet's cousin is a native of that city.

clue.text: Key producer with little time to spare in museum

parts.note: the ash tree produces winged seeds called keys
MO, a moment, is a little time
spare and lean both mean thin

explanation.surface: A locksmith with a few minutes free inside a museum.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashmolean is Oxford University's museum of art and archaeology.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper name of the Oxford institution of art and archaeology, Britain's oldest public one of its kind.

clue.text: Clever man at Oxford, according to Toad?

definitions.text: Clever man at Oxford, according to Toad?

parts.words: Clever man at Oxford, according to Toad?
parts.note: Toad's boastful song in The Wind in the Willows says the clever men at Oxford know everything there is to be knowed

explanation.surface: Toad of Toad Hall gives his opinion of a brainy Oxford don.
explanation.walkthrough: In Kenneth Grahame's The Wind in the Willows, Toad sings that the clever men at Oxford know all there is to know, but not half as much as he.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who claims to have every fact at their fingertips, like the Oxford men in Toad's song.

clue.text: Round object, nothing like Humpty Dumpty

parts.note: the letter O is shaped like a ring, a round object
a void is emptiness, nothing

explanation.surface: A ball that looks nothing like the nursery-rhyme egg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nothing like' reads as 'unlike', but 'nothing' gives VOID and 'like Humpty Dumpty' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Humpty Dumpty is an egg, and egg-shaped means oval in form.

clue.text: William's father was a policeman

explanation.surface: A family history note: William's dad served in the police force.
explanation.walkthrough: William the Conqueror's father was Robert, Duke of Normandy; Robert (after Sir Robert Peel, founder of the London police) is old British slang for a policeman, like bobby.
explanation.definitionFit: Historical fact for the Conqueror's parent, and dated British slang naming a constable after Sir Robert Peel.

clue.text: Source of fruit or vegetable

parts.note: chard is a leafy vegetable

explanation.surface: Where fruit or vegetables come from.
explanation.definitionFit: A plantation of fruit trees is where apples and pears come from.

clue.text: Character found in Genesis, chapter one? Wrong

indicators.note: set wrong means put into the wrong order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A query whether a figure appears in the first chapter of Genesis, answered no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong' rearranges CH and ONE. The figure appears in Genesis chapter 4 and 5, not chapter one.
explanation.definitionFit: Father of Methuselah, a patriarch named in the early genealogies of the first book of the Bible.

clue.text: Accept a course in such a restaurant

parts.note: to take something is to accept it
a way is a course or route

explanation.surface: Agree to have one course of a meal at this kind of eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' looks like a dish, but it is a route.
explanation.definitionFit: An eatery selling food to be eaten off the premises, a carry-out shop.

clue.text: Correspondingly your servant could be so biddable

definitions.text: Correspondingly your servant could be so

explanation.surface: A formal letter sign-off describes a servant as docile.
explanation.walkthrough: Old formal letters ended 'Your obedient servant'; 'Correspondingly' means in correspondence, letter-writing.
explanation.definitionFit: The old letter closing names a servant who does as told, and biddable means docile and compliant.

clue.text: Somehow or other, using bent pin or curved stick

definitions.text: using bent pin or curved stick

explanation.surface: Someone improvises a fishing tool from a bent pin or a curved stick.
explanation.walkthrough: A hook is a bent pin and a crook is a curved stick, so the second half is a literal reading of the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning by any means available; literally, with a hook or with a shepherd's crook.

clue.text: Creature spotted by Ethiopian

parts.note: recalls Jeremiah 13:23, 'Can the Ethiopian change his skin, or the big cat his spots?': the animal is spotted, and is mentioned beside the Ethiopian

explanation.surface: An animal was sighted by a man from Ethiopia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted' seems to mean seen, but it means bearing spots; the Biblical verse pairs the Ethiopian with this animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A big cat with a spotted coat, named alongside the Ethiopian in the Bible verse about unchangeable nature.

clue.text: Money for short part of book put into play

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside another, as the clue says the part of a book goes into the play

parts.note: a play is a drama
CH is the short form of chapter, a part of a book

explanation.surface: Someone pays for a shortened section of a book to be adapted for the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The currency of Greece before the euro, so a unit of money.

clue.text: Admiral set one firm course

parts.note: jelly sets, or jells, when it firms up
I is the Roman numeral for one
CO is short for company, a firm
E, east, is a compass course to steer

explanation.surface: A naval commander sets a single steady course for the fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: John Jellicoe commanded the British Grand Fleet at Jutland in 1916.
explanation.definitionFit: Surname of the British naval commander at the Battle of Jutland, a senior flag officer.

clue.text: Between them they carry another lot of Presidents

explanation.surface: A group sharing a load is a different set of heads of state.
explanation.walkthrough: Sedan chairs were carried by a pair of bearers; 'another lot of' marks a second sense: company heads.
explanation.definitionFit: Bearers of a sedan chair carried it between them; heads of boards or meetings are also called presidents.

clue.text: Principle to follow, to a degree

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
MA, Master of Arts, is a university degree

explanation.surface: A rule of conduct that should be followed, at least partially.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to a degree' looks like 'somewhat' but supplies MA.
explanation.definitionFit: A firmly held tenet or doctrine, a principle accepted without question.

clue.text: Reddish-orange fabric

explanation.surface: Cloth of a warm red-orange shade.
explanation.definitionFit: A colour named after pomegranate syrup, and a thin open-weave dress material of silk or wool.

clue.text: Invective cut short in battle

indicators.note: something cut short loses its end, so the last letter of the speech word goes

parts.note: a philippic is a bitter verbal attack, invective

explanation.surface: Abusive language is broken off during a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Philippi in Macedonia was where Antony and Octavian defeated Brutus and Cassius in 42 BC.
explanation.definitionFit: Site of the 42 BC clash where Brutus and Cassius were defeated, a famous ancient engagement.

clue.text: Crew got from deck

explanation.surface: Sailors were taken off the ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck' means the ship's floor in the surface but a pack of cards in the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers aboard a ship are its crew; card players are dealt their sets of cards from the pack.

clue.text: Meat course nothing if not this

explanation.surface: A meat dish described as something above all else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not a sausage' is British slang for nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A banger is a meat dish; 'not a sausage' is a British idiom meaning nothing.

clue.text: Perhaps a daughter is bound by written contract

parts.note: the word a is an example of an article in grammar, hence perhaps

explanation.surface: Someone's daughter may be bound by a formal written agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' looks like part of 'a daughter' but is the grammatical article.
explanation.definitionFit: Apprentices and trainee solicitors were indentured under formal articles, bound by contract to a master.

clue.text: Part of church fortune increased by pound

indicators.note: one piece is enlarged by having another added after it

parts.note: fortune and chance both mean luck
L is the abbreviation for pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A church's wealth grew by a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fortune' suggests wealth but means luck.
explanation.definitionFit: The area near the altar reserved for clergy and choir, a section of a church building.

clue.text: Inscription on side edge

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
an end is an extremity or edge

explanation.surface: Writing found along a side edge, as on a coin.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side, also called the leg side, is the half of the field behind the batsman's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: The writing around a coin or under a picture, an inscription or caption.

clue.text: Have-not, we hear, in Japan

indicators.note: says the word for one who lacks is to be heard, not read

parts.note: a have-not is someone who lacks things, a lacker

explanation.surface: A poor person living in Japan, so we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Japan' with a capital is the country in the surface, but japan is a hard glossy varnish.
explanation.definitionFit: Japan is a black glossy varnish of the Japanese kind, a synonym for this coating.

clue.text: Unhappy announcer?

parts.note: one who weeps is unhappy, and a town official making proclamations is also called by the same word

explanation.surface: A gloomy broadcaster.
explanation.definitionFit: One who weeps, and the town official who shouted public proclamations.

clue.text: The riddle of amateur dramatics

parts.note: a word puzzle acted out syllable by syllable, a parlour game of home theatricals

explanation.surface: The mystery behind a village drama society.
explanation.definitionFit: A party game where players act out a word for others to guess, a riddle in mime.

clue.text: Grave is right in hollow

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other, as right is said to be in the hollow

parts.note: a cave is a hollow in rock

explanation.surface: A tomb is properly located in a cavity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave' looks like a noun, tomb, but is the old verb meaning engrave.
explanation.definitionFit: To grave is an old verb meaning to engrave or cut into, as with a sculptor's chisel.

clue.text: Doctor's work making Tommy perfect?

explanation.surface: A doctor's job is to turn a British soldier into a model specimen.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy is a British private soldier, and practice makes perfect.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicine done for paying patients outside the state health service; whimsically, the drilling of a soldier to perfection.

clue.text: Country naming 18 as pirate

explanation.surface: A nation names a crewman as a pirate.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 across is HANDS; Israel Hands is a pirate in Stevenson's Treasure Island.
explanation.definitionFit: A Middle Eastern nation, and the first name of the buccaneer in Treasure Island.

clue.text: We will study to become this

definitions.text: We will study to become this

parts.note: contracted, we will is we'll
to read a subject is to study it

explanation.surface: Students vow to study hard so as to become learned.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone widely versed in books is learned, which is what studying makes you.
